content: No, that is not true. In Switzerland, if a popular initiative is accepted by the people in a national vote, it becomes part of the Swiss Federal Constitution and must be implemented by the Federal Assembly (the Swiss parliament) and the Federal Council (the Swiss government). Neither the parliament nor the Federal Council can reject or block a popular initiative that has been approved by the people. They are legally bound to enact the necessary legislation to give effect to the initiative within a reasonable timeframe.
